findings.title: The abstract awards the deployed configuration a win record that belongs to the other arm
findings.where: paper2/grail_service.tex lines 37–39 (rendered PDF: "Against MetaTox the deployed configuration leads at every budget, with the interval separating at seven of nine, while emitting 15.7 candidates against MetaTox's 31.")
findings.problem: Two different arms are fused into one sentence. The paper itself defines the deployed configuration as the trained rule budget (§'The emitted set', line 216: "the service returns what the trained rule budget produces"), and that is the arm emitting 15.7. But the trained budget does NOT lead at every budget: it trails MetaTox at k=20, 30 and 50 with paired-bootstrap intervals that exclude zero. 'Leads at every budget, separating at seven of nine' is true only of the whole-bank arm, which emits 98.9, not 15.7. The paper's own generated claim block (paper2/claim.tex) states both records correctly and separately; the abstract, which is hand-written, merges them. The preregistration §0.2b anticipates exactly this error verbatim: "Written by hand it was wrong within the hour: it said the point estimate leads at k=15 and k=20, which is true of the whole bank and false of the trained budget."
findings.evidence: results/deployment_table.json contrasts: trained budget − metatox = −0.0647 [−0.1050, −0.0251] at k=20, −0.1113 [−0.1523, −0.0706] at k=30, −0.1368 [−0.1846, −0.0917] at k=50, all excludes_zero=true; whole bank − metatox positive at all nine k with excludes_zero=true at 1,3,5,8,10,30,50. mean_output_length: whole bank 98.9, trained budget 15.7. paper2/claim.tex lines 1–3.
findings.fix: Rewrite the abstract sentence to name the arm for each fact, e.g. 'the whole-bank configuration leads at every budget (interval excluding zero at seven of nine) while emitting 98.9 candidates; the deployed trained budget leads at k≤10 emitting 15.7 and trails with the interval excluding zero at k=20, 30 and 50.' Generate this sentence from deployment_table.json the same way claim.tex is generated, so it cannot drift.
findings.why_it_survived: Verified. grail_service.tex:37-39 reads "the deployed configuration leads at every budget, with the interval separating at seven of nine, while emitting \numOutputTrained candidates against MetaTox's \numOutputMetatox" (15.7 vs 31). The paper defines the deployed configuration at line 216 as "the service returns what the trained rule budget produces", and numbers.tex:176 gives output.trained = 15.7 to that arm. results/deployment_table.json contrasts show 'trained budget - metatox' gaps of -0.0647 [-0.1050,-0.0251] at k=20, -0.1113 [-0.1523,-0.0706] at k=30 and -0.1368 [-0.1846,-0.0917] at k=50, all excludes_zero=true, so the trained budget does not lead at every budget and separates against the paper at three of nine. 'Seven of nine' is exactly the whole bank's record (excludes_zero at 1,3,5,8,10,30,50), and that arm emits 98.9, not 15.7. So the sentence is false under either arm reading; the two arms are fused. paper2/claim.tex:1-3, generated from the artifact, states both records correctly and separately, and preregistration.md 0.2b records the identical hand-written error being caught once already ("it said the point estimate leads at k=15 and k=20, which is true of the whole bank and false of the trained budget"). This is the abstract's central comparative claim, so fatal stands.

findings.title: The Limitations section states the opposite of the paper's own comparison table at k=20, 30 and 50
findings.where: paper2/grail_service.tex lines 285–286: "At a budget of fifteen and above, the interval on the difference to MetaTox does not separate for either configuration. We report the point estimates and the intervals and make no claim there."
findings.problem: False for six of the eight (arm, budget) cells at k ≥ 15. The trained budget's interval excludes zero AGAINST the paper at k=20, 30 and 50; the whole bank's excludes zero FOR the paper at k=30 and 50. Only k=15 (both arms) and k=20 (whole bank) fail to separate. The sentence converts a mixed picture — in which the deployed configuration is significantly worse than the comparator at three of nine budgets — into a blanket 'no claim', and it contradicts paper2/claim.tex printed two pages earlier in the same document, which says the trained budget "trails with the interval excluding zero at k = 20, 30 and 50."
findings.evidence: results/deployment_table.json → contrasts.20/30/50 'trained budget - metatox' excludes_zero: true (gaps −0.0647, −0.1113, −0.1368); contrasts.30/50 'whole bank - metatox' excludes_zero: true (gaps +0.0391, +0.0797). paper2/claim.tex line 3.
findings.fix: Replace with the truth: 'At k=15 neither arm separates, and at k=20 the whole bank does not. At k=20, 30 and 50 the trained budget trails MetaTox with the interval excluding zero; at k=30 and 50 the whole bank leads with the interval excluding zero.' Then state what the deployed arm's significant deficit at wide budgets means for a user who reads fifty candidates.
findings.why_it_survived: Verified as a false statement, downgraded from fatal because the paper states the truth elsewhere. grail_service.tex:314-315: "At a budget of fifteen and above, the interval on the difference to MetaTox does not separate for either configuration. We report the point estimates and the intervals and make no claim there." results/deployment_table.json: at k=20/30/50 'trained budget - metatox' excludes_zero=true (-0.0647, -0.1113, -0.1368) and at k=30/50 'whole bank - metatox' excludes_zero=true (+0.0391, +0.0797). Only three of the eight (arm, budget) cells at k>=15 fail to separate, so the sentence is wrong for six, and wrong in the direction that spares the deployed arm a significant deficit in the section whose job is to disclose it. It also contradicts claim.tex:3 inserted at line 205 of the same document ("It trails with the interval excluding zero at k = 20, 30 and 50"), and the abstract's own claim of separation at 30 and 50. Not fatal because the adverse result is printed verbatim by the artifact-generated claim block two pages earlier and the body text at line 207-208 says "Above ten it trails" - a reader of the whole paper is not deceived, but the sentence must be corrected.

findings.title: The cost decomposition inverts its artifact: 13.9 is the enumeration collapse factor, not standardisation's share
findings.where: paper2/grail_service.tex line 72–73 (Introduction bullet) and line 264: "Standardising the enumerated products takes the rest: it is $\numHOneThreeEnumeration$ times the remaining work"
findings.problem: 13.9 is not that quantity. The artifact key is literally named enumeration_alone_against_the_old_total and equals median(old whole-product total 49.85 s) / median(new arm's enumeration 3.59 s). The producing script writes its own reading of the number: "enumeration collapses by 13.9 times, and standardising the hundred survivors is 72 per cent of what remains, so the arm as a whole moves by 2.95". The quantity the manuscript claims — standardisation over the rest — is share_spent_standardising = 0.717, i.e. a ratio of about 2.5, not 13.9. Even read as total/rest, 13.9 would imply part/rest = 12.9, not 13.9. The manuscript inflates its second headline contribution by roughly 5.5×.
findings.evidence: results/h13_verdict.json → time.enumeration_alone_against_the_old_total = 13.9; time.every_product_median_s = 49.85; time.inside_survivors.enumerate_median_s = 3.59, standardise_survivors_median_s = 11.88, share_spent_standardising = 0.717. scripts/typed_edit/h13_verdict.py lines 120–126 ("reading" field).
findings.fix: State the quantity the artifact measures: standardising the survivors is 72% of the survivors arm's time, about 2.5 times its enumeration; and enumeration alone is 13.9 times faster than the old whole-product total. Add a macro for share_spent_standardising and stop reusing h13.enumeration for a different claim.
findings.why_it_survived: The defect is real but far smaller than claimed. results/h13_verdict.json time.enumeration_alone_against_the_old_total = 13.9, and scripts/typed_edit/h13_verdict.py:119-120 computes it as round(median(A)/median(enum),1) = 49.85/3.59, i.e. the OLD whole-product arm's total over the NEW arm's enumeration step. grail_service.tex:72-73 and 292-293 gloss it as standardisation over "the remaining work" / "the rest of the generator's work", which is (49.85-3.59)/3.59 = 12.9, not 13.9. So the manuscript prints a whole/part ratio while describing a part/rest one. But the finding's own quantification is refuted: share_spent_standardising = 0.717 is measured inside the SURVIVORS arm, where only the ~100 capped survivors are standardised, and the manuscript's sentence is explicitly about the old arm ("run once per product of every template, about four thousand times per substrate"). The correct figure in the sense the manuscript uses is ~12.9, not ~2.5, so there is no 5.5x inflation and the qualitative claim - standardisation dominates the generator's cost - is untouched. What survives is a number that does not mean what its sentence says, off by about 8 per cent: worth a one-line correction, not a fatal finding.

findings.title: "MetaTox is read from its own predictions with no cap imposed by us" is false; the harness truncates it at 50
findings.where:
paper2/grail_service.tex lines 180–182: "MetaTox is read from its own predictions with no cap imposed by us. Mean list lengths are $
umOutputBank$, $
umOutputTrained$ and $
umOutputMetatox$ respectively." (98.9, 15.7, 31)
findings.problem: The script that produces the table calls `_dedup(mtx.get(s, []), max(KS))` with max(KS)=50, so every MetaTox list is truncated to 50 keys before anything is measured. The 31.0 in the abstract and in §Comparison is a post-truncation mean; MetaTox's actual deduplicated emission on these 291 substrates is 36.34 (results/h11_grid.json), and 249 of its 291 lists are already shorter than 50, so the truncation moves the mean by 5.3 on the 42 longest lists. The sentence asserting that no cap was imposed is contradicted by the code that wrote the number in the same sentence, and the understated 31 flatters the abstract's efficiency claim ('15.7 against 31').
findings.evidence: scripts/typed_edit/deployment_table.py line 75: `"metatox": {s: _dedup(mtx.get(s, []), max(KS)) for s in subs}`, with KS = (1,3,5,8,10,15,20,30,50) and `_dedup(smiles, cap)` in scripts/bank_without_selection.py lines 137–150 stopping at cap. results/deployment_table.json mean_output_length.metatox = 31.0; results/h11_grid.json mean_output.metatox = 36.34; substrates_whose_list_is_shorter_than_the_budget.50.metatox = 249.
findings.fix: Either drop the 50-cap on MetaTox for the list-length statistic and report 36.34, or keep it and say so ('MetaTox's lists are truncated at 50, the widest budget reported; its untruncated mean is 36.34'). The recall columns are unaffected, but every sentence comparing emitted volume must use the untruncated figure.
findings.why_it_survived: The truncation is real and the methods sentence is false, but the consequence is the opposite of the one alleged. scripts/typed_edit/deployment_table.py:75 builds the MetaTox arm as _dedup(mtx.get(s,[]), max(KS)) with KS topping out at 50, and scripts/bank_without_selection.py:139-151 stops at the cap, so grail_service.tex:180-181 ("MetaTox is read from its own predictions with no cap imposed by us") is contradicted by the code that produced the number in the same sentence - as is the script's own docstring. The reported mean_output_length.metatox = 31.0 is therefore post-truncation, while the same paper prints 36.34 for MetaTox's mean output at line 217-218 (\numHOneOneOutputMetatox, results/h11_grid.json) with no reconciliation. Refuted, however: (a) no recall or interval is affected, since the largest reported budget is 50 and truncation at 50 cannot change recall@k for k<=50, and the shorter-than-budget counts are likewise unchanged; (b) the claim that the understated 31 "flatters the abstract's efficiency claim" is backwards - a smaller MetaTox list makes GRAIL's 15.7 look LESS efficient, so the error runs against the authors' interest; (c) all three arms are bounded (the GRAIL arms by the disclosed H9 cap of 100, which is why the bank reports 98.9). Residual defect: a false clause in Methods plus an internal 31-vs-36.34 inconsistency. Minor.

findings.title: "The cap was expected to cost recall" contradicts the preregistration, which predicted a gain
findings.where: paper2/grail_service.tex lines 132–133: "The cap was expected to cost recall and to be adopted anyway, since it bounds the filter's work. It gains instead."
findings.problem: The preregistration predicts the opposite, in the registered direction and with a registered margin: "On the validation split, micro recall@15 under the cap exceeds micro recall@15 without it by at least +0.015", and it says outright "Measured on the 291, the cap does not cost recall; it gains" and "the registration's own prediction is that this costs nothing." A paper whose first contribution bullet is that it fixes each rule in a preregistration before checking it then narrates the registered prediction backwards to manufacture a surprise. Separately, the same prereg section states that the cap does not deliver the cost saving the manuscript attributes to it: "A pool cannot be capped before it has been enumerated, so this cap saves nothing on the cost that actually grows" — which the manuscript's own §Cost confirms (the cost is in the generator's standardisation, not the filter), yet line 132 justifies the cap by 'it bounds the filter's work'.
findings.evidence: paper2/preregistration.md §H9 (lines ~523–560): 'Prediction. On the validation split, micro recall@15 under the cap exceeds micro recall@15 without it by at least +0.015… Failure: the margin is below +0.015, or negative.'; 'What this cap does not bound… this cap saves nothing on the cost that actually grows.' results/h9_verdict.json registered_threshold = 0.015, note = 'The cap is adopted as a cost guard whichever way this falls; only the claim that it improves the ranking is decided here.'
findings.fix: Replace with the registered story: 'The cap was registered to gain at least +0.015 and to be adopted as a filter-side guard regardless; it gained +0.026.' And state the prereg's own finding that the cap does not touch the generator-side cost that actually grows.
findings.why_it_survived: First charge verified, second refuted. grail_service.tex:132-133 says "The cap was expected to cost recall and to be adopted anyway... It gains instead." preregistration.md H9 registers the opposite direction with a margin: "On the validation split, micro recall@15 under the cap exceeds micro recall@15 without it by at least +0.015... Failure: the margin is below +0.015, or negative", plus "Measured on the 291, the cap does not cost recall; it gains" and "the registration's own prediction is that this costs nothing"; results/h9_verdict.json carries registered_threshold 0.015 in the positive direction. The manuscript narrates the registered prediction backwards to manufacture a surprise, in the paper whose first contribution bullet is that each rule is fixed in a preregistration before checking. That is a claim contradicted by a released artifact and must be fixed. The second charge fails: the prereg itself justifies the cap exactly as the manuscript does - "what H9 bounds is the filter's share" and "bounding the pool at 100 bounds the filter's work by six times on the mean and forty-six on the worst substrate". The prereg's "this cap saves nothing on the cost that actually grows" is about the generator's cost, which the manuscript's Cost section locates correctly and never attributes to the cap. Major rather than fatal: no number or interval changes, and the released preregistration lets a reader see the true direction.

findings.title: The abstract and §3.2 print a recall value where the cap size belongs
findings.where: paper2/grail_service.tex line 31 (abstract) "capping the candidate pool at $\numHNineCapped$ … before ranking" and line 127 "Keeping the $\numHNineCapped$ highest by generator score before ranking"; rendered PDF: "capping the candidate pool at 0.4748"
findings.problem: \numHNineCapped is h9.capped = 0.4748, the micro recall@15 under the cap, not the cap size. The cap is 100. The same macro is then used correctly three words later in line 128 ('raises micro recall@15 from 0.4489 to 0.4748'), so line 127 reads 'Keeping the 0.4748 highest by generator score … raises micro recall@15 from 0.4489 to 0.4748'. The cap's actual value, 100, appears nowhere in the manuscript, and numbers.tex has no macro for it — so the paper's second headline change is never quantified.
findings.evidence: paper2/numbers.tex line 143: \newcommand{\numHNineCapped}{0.4748} % h9.capped. results/h9_verdict.json: "cap": 100, micro.capped = 0.4748. pdftotext output of paper2/grail_service.pdf: 'capping the candidate pool at 0.47481 before ranking'.
findings.fix: Add \numHNineCap = 100 sourced from h9_verdict.json's `cap` field and use it in both places. Add a paper2 numeral-coverage check (scripts/check_coverage.py currently reads only paper/grail_iclr.tex, so no gate looks at this file).
findings.why_it_survived:
VERIFIED. paper2/numbers.tex:159 defines 
umHNineCapped as 0.4748 with the trailing key `% h9.capped`, and results/h9_verdict.json records micro.capped = 0.4748 with a separate top-level field "cap": 100. The macro is used in a cap-size slot twice: paper2/grail_service.tex:30-31 ("capping the candidate pool at $
umHNineCapped$ ... before ranking is worth a further $
umHNineDiff$") and :126-128 ("Keeping the $
umHNineCapped$ highest by generator score before ranking ... raises micro recall@15 from $
umHNineUncapped$ to $
umHNineCapped$"). pdftotext of paper2/grail_service.pdf confirms the rendering: the abstract prints "capping the candidate pool at 0.47481" (the trailing 1 is the footnote marker) and section 3.2 prints "Keeping the 0.4748 highest by generator score ... raises micro recall@15 from 0.4489 to 0.4748". The same macro therefore carries two incompatible meanings in one sentence, and the second occurrence is a self-referential tautology. No refutation available: no other macro in numbers.tex holds 100 (grep confirms), so the cap cannot be printed as written. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE FINDING, neither of which saves the manuscript: (a) the cap value is not entirely absent from the paper -- grail_service.tex:294 says "about four thousand times per substrate to keep the hundred that survive the cap", so 100 appears once, in prose, in the Cost section; (b) 
umHNinePoolAfter (98) does quantify the post-cap pool in the abstract, so the change is partly quantified. SEVERITY DOWNGRADED from fatal to major: this is an unambiguous macro misuse producing a nonsense sentence in the abstract and in the section whose job is to define the cap, and it must be fixed before submission, but it does not misstate a result in the authors' favour -- every recall figure it prints is the correct one from h9_verdict.json, and no conclusion changes.

findings.title: The ordering-headroom diagnosis is baselined against a ranking the paper never deploys and never identifies
findings.where:
paper2/grail_service.tex lines 153–155 "Handing the ranker a perfect choice of formula group lifts micro recall@15 from $
umOracleAsranked$ to $
umOracleBetween$" (0.3549 → 0.6692) and lines 288–290 "The between-group ordering headroom, worth $
umOracleBetween$ against $
umOracleAsranked$ under an oracle, is not reached by either composition we registered."
findings.problem: 0.3549 is the `as_ranked` arm of wide_pool_analysis, which is neither the deployed ranker nor even the product ranking: the code sorts by the product score, regroups candidates by molecular formula, and emits each formula group contiguously. It is the product ranking blocked by formula — the very layout the paper independently measures as costing −0.0647 (§3.4, line 164: 'the same fusion ranking blocked that way is worse than interleaved'). On the same uncapped pool and same 291 substrates the un-blocked product scores 0.3759 and the fusion rule 0.5023; the deployed configuration scores 0.5353. The real headroom over the deployed ranker is 0.134, not 0.314. The Limitations sentence then charges the registered compositions with failing to close a gap that is more than half composed of the blocking penalty and the product-to-fusion step the paper's own H7 already closed (H12's three-way reaches 0.5308).
findings.evidence: scripts/typed_edit/wide_pool_analysis.py lines ~92–113: `cands = sorted(pools[s], key=lambda c: -c["combined"])`; groups by `formula`; `by_score = sorted(groups, key=lambda g: best[g])`; `orders = {"as_ranked": flat(by_score, plain), ...}`. results/wide_pool_analysis_implicit.json: arms.as_ranked.recall@15_micro = 0.3549, arms.oracle_between = 0.6692, score_combinations_at_15_micro = {product 0.3759, generator 0.4271, rrf 0.5023}, mean_pool 588.7 (uncapped). results/deployment_table.json recall_micro.15 whole bank = 0.5353. results/h8_verdict.json what_the_design_costs_before_the_model_acts = −0.0647.
findings.fix: Report the oracle contrast against the ranking the paper actually uses — fusion on the capped pool — or state explicitly that `as_ranked` is the product ordering blocked by formula group on the uncapped 588.7-deep pool, and give the headroom over fusion (0.6692 − 0.5023) as the number the registered compositions were trying to close.
findings.why_it_survived: VERIFIED. scripts/typed_edit/wide_pool_analysis.py builds `as_ranked` as flat(by_score, plain): candidates are sorted by c["combined"] (the product score), grouped by molecular formula, groups ordered by the index of their best member, and each group's members emitted contiguously. That is the product ranking with formula blocking imposed -- not the deployed ranking and not even the plain product ranking. The same artifact separates the two: results/wide_pool_analysis_implicit.json gives arms.as_ranked.recall@15_micro = 0.3549 while score_combinations_at_15_micro.product = 0.3759 and .rrf = 0.5023, on the same 291 substrates and the same uncapped mean_pool 588.7. results/deployment_table.json puts the deployed whole bank at 0.5353 at k=15 on that identical population (its gate field reproduces_four_method_291_metatox = true confirms population/criterion match). The manuscript prints 0.3549 with no identification at grail_service.tex:153-155 ("Handing the ranker a perfect choice of formula group lifts micro recall@15 from 0.3549 to 0.6692"), so a reader arriving from section 3.1 (fusion 0.4489) and 3.2 (capped 0.4748) has no way to know the baseline is a layout the paper elsewhere rejects. The Limitations sentence at :317-319 is the load-bearing defect: it charges "either composition we registered" with not reaching a headroom of 0.6692 against 0.3549, while both registered compositions (H8, H12) are measured against interleaved fusion at 0.5023 (results/h8_verdict.json recall_micro.15.fusion, results/h12_verdict.json two_way). The headroom over the ranking the paper actually deploys is 0.1669 on the matched uncapped pool (0.6692 - 0.5023), roughly half of the 0.3143 implied. The authors already know this: paper2/preregistration.md:503-505 states "The +0.1729 of oracle headroom this hypothesis was built on was measured in the blocked form, so its first 0.0647 was never headroom at all" -- and grail_service.tex:164-166 independently reports the -0.0647 blocking cost, which makes the Limitations sentence internally inconsistent with section 3.4. Attempted refutations that fail: (a) "all four oracle arms share as_ranked as their control, so the within-vs-between decomposition is matched" -- true for the decomposition, and that part of :153-156 survives, but it does not license the cross-baseline claim at :317-319; (b) "0.3549 is just the product ranking" -- refuted by the artifact, which reports product separately at 0.3759. SEVERITY DOWNGRADED from fatal to major: the qualitative conclusion (neither registered composition reaches the between-group oracle) is still true at the correct baseline -- H12's third-term nudge is +0.0286 against a real 0.1669 gap -- so no conclusion reverses; what is defective is the unlabelled baseline and a headroom overstated by about a factor of two in the one place the paper concedes a limitation.

findings.title: oracle_third is called "a perfect group ranking" and used to conclude boundedness, which both its artifact and the preregistration disclaim
findings.where:
paper2/grail_service.tex lines 169–172: "It is worth $
umHOneTwoDiff$ $[
umHOneTwoLo, 
umHOneTwoHi]$, and a \emph{perfect} group ranking entered the same way is worth $
umHOneTwoCeiling$: a reciprocal-rank term is bounded, so however good the group ordering is it can only nudge."
findings.problem: oracle_third is not a perfect group ranking and is not an upper bound. Its own artifact says so in a field named ceiling_note: "oracle_third ranks groups binarily, so it orders nothing among the groups holding no reference; a graded ranking can and does exceed it, and a share above one means that rather than the model beating an upper bound." The preregistration devotes a paragraph to it titled 'Where `oracle_third` stops being a ceiling', and on the validation split the trained scorer exceeds it (0.4901 vs 0.4748; share_of_ceiling_taken = 1.5846, margin +0.0412 against the 'ceiling' 0.0260). The manuscript takes a coincidental equality on one population (share = 1.0 on the 291) and derives a boundedness conclusion that the held-out measurement falsifies. The 'ceiling' also carries an interval, [0.0156, 0.0431], which is not printed.
findings.evidence: results/h12_verdict.json: ceiling_of_this_composition = {gap 0.0286, ci95 [0.0156, 0.0431]}, share_of_ceiling_taken = 1.0, ceiling_note as quoted. results/h12_verdict_validation.json: primary gap 0.0412 [0.0192, 0.0621], ceiling_of_this_composition 0.0260, share_of_ceiling_taken 1.5846. paper2/preregistration.md §H12, subsection 'Where `oracle_third` stops being a ceiling' and '`oracle_third` is exceeded on validation, which settles what it is.'
findings.fix: Drop the word 'perfect' and the boundedness inference. State what the artifact states: oracle_third is a binary group ordering, not an upper bound, and a graded scorer exceeds it on validation (0.0412 against 0.0260). If a boundedness claim about reciprocal-rank terms is wanted, derive it analytically rather than from this arm.
findings.why_it_survived:
VERIFIED. grail_service.tex:169-172 reads "It is worth $
umHOneTwoDiff$ $[
umHOneTwoLo, 
umHOneTwoHi]$, and a \emph{perfect} group ranking entered the same way is worth $
umHOneTwoCeiling$: a reciprocal-rank term is bounded, so however good the group ordering is it can only nudge." The 0.0286/0.0286 equality is correctly read off results/h12_verdict.json (primary gap 0.0286, ceiling_of_this_composition.gap 0.0286, share_of_ceiling_taken 1.0). But the same artifact carries a field named ceiling_note that disclaims the reading the manuscript builds on it: "oracle_third ranks groups binarily, so it orders nothing among the groups holding no reference; a graded ranking can and does exceed it, and a share above one means that rather than the model beating an upper bound." results/h12_verdict_validation.json is the counterexample at the same budget: three_way 0.4901 against oracle_third 0.4748 at k=15, primary gap 0.0412 against ceiling_of_this_composition 0.0260, share_of_ceiling_taken 1.5846. So the arm is exceeded on the other population at the very budget the paper reports, which kills even the narrow defence the preregistration offers at paper2/preregistration.md:820-824 ("It bounds only the budget at which knowing which groups hold a reference is the whole question"). The preregistration devotes two headed paragraphs to this -- "Where `oracle_third` stops being a ceiling" and "`oracle_third` is exceeded on validation, which settles what it is" ("An arm that can be beaten is not an upper bound") -- and none of it reaches the manuscript. The finding's secondary point is also correct: h12_verdict.json's ceiling carries ci95 [0.0156, 0.0431] and the paper prints an interval on the primary gap only. Attempted refutations that fail: (a) "the prereg itself calls it a perfect group ranking" -- it does at line 812, but it then retracts the ceiling reading in the two paragraphs that follow, and the paper keeps the retracted half; (b) "the boundedness argument is structural, not empirical" -- the sentence's colon presents the oracle equality as the evidence for it, and the k>=20 rows of h12_verdict.json (three_way 0.5865/0.6421/0.6917 against oracle_third 0.5729/0.6195/0.6827) show the arm beaten at three more budgets. SEVERITY DOWNGRADED from fatal to major: the surviving magnitude claim (this composition nudges, +0.0286 held out, +0.0412 on validation) is not disturbed, so the paper's account of H12 as a small real effect stands; what must go is the word "perfect", the ceiling framing, and the unqualified "can only nudge", each of which the released artifact contradicts in a field written by the authors' own script.

findings.title: Three comparators with predictions on the identical 291 substrates are unreported, and two of them lead both GRAIL arms at the tight budgets the paper motivates
findings.where: paper2/grail_service.tex §2.1 lines 98–102 and §4 lines 177–211 (Table 1); results/four_method_291.json
findings.problem: The artifact that DEFINES the population — results/four_method_291.json, named as "the 291 of results/four_method_291.json" in deployment_table.json, h8_verdict.json, h12_verdict.json and h14_verdict.json — carries SyGMa and MetaPredictor predictions on exactly these substrates, computed under the same matching criterion (inchikey_tautomer), the same aggregation (micro, ratio of sums) and the same budget grid. Both beat both GRAIL configurations at k = 1, 3, 5, and MetaPredictor and SyGMa also beat the whole bank at k = 8 and 10. MetaTox is the weakest of the three at exactly the budgets where the paper claims its lead. The manuscript names none of them, and the project's own preregistration (paper2/preregistration.md §0.3) states the rule it breaks: "A comparator that cannot be obtained by the freeze is reported in the paper as unavailable, with the reason; it is not silently dropped."
findings.evidence: four_method_291.json per_method recall (micro, same 291, same criterion): SyGMa {1:0.1534, 3:0.2887, 5:0.3744, 8:0.4271, 10:0.4556}; MetaPredictor {1:0.1398, 3:0.2767, 5:0.3549, 8:0.4346, 10:0.4707}; MetaTox {1:0.0406, 3:0.1323, 5:0.2180}. deployment_table.json: whole bank {1:0.0902, 3:0.2271, 5:0.3098, 8:0.4135, 10:0.4496}, trained budget {1:0.1053, 3:0.2406, 5:0.3188, 8:0.4015, 10:0.4331}. The same artifact's robust_order records "MetaPredictor over GRAIL: dominates true, certified true, budgets_that_reverse_it []" and "SyGMa over GRAIL: dominates true, certified true".
findings.fix: Either extend Table 1 to every comparator whose frozen predictions exist on the 291 (SyGMa, MetaPredictor at minimum) with the paired interval on each difference, or state explicitly in §2.1 and §4 that only MetaTox is compared, why, and that two available comparators lead at k ≤ 10 — and remove the screening-at-three-candidates framing that the omitted arms refute.
findings.why_it_survived: VERIFIED, and the comparison is matched, which is what makes it actionable. results/four_method_291.json config declares n_substrates 291, match "inchikey_tautomer", aggregation "micro, ratio of sums", the same nine-budget k_sweep, and population "the 291 MetaTox submission substrates, all of which carry references and predictions from every method here". results/deployment_table.json names the same source ("the 291 of results/four_method_291.json"), the same aggregation, and carries a gate field reproduces_four_method_291_metatox = true with mismatches [] -- the two artifacts agree on the MetaTox column cell for cell, so their other columns are directly comparable. Side by side (bank / trained / SyGMa / MetaPredictor): k=1 0.0902 / 0.1053 / 0.1534 / 0.1398; k=3 0.2271 / 0.2406 / 0.2887 / 0.2767; k=5 0.3098 / 0.3188 / 0.3744 / 0.3549; k=8 0.4135 / 0.4015 / 0.4271 / 0.4346; k=10 0.4496 / 0.4331 / 0.4556 / 0.4707. Both comparators lead both GRAIL arms at all five budgets at or below ten -- one more budget than the finding claims -- including k=3, the budget grail_service.tex:62 names as the motivating case ("A screening application reads three candidates"). MetaTox is the weakest of the three across that whole range. The manuscript names neither: grep over grail_service.tex and claim.tex returns no occurrence of SyGMa, MetaPredictor or BioTransformer, though refs.bib carries all three entries uncited. paper2/preregistration.md:236-238 states the rule this breaks -- "A comparator that cannot be obtained by the freeze is reported in the paper as unavailable, with the reason; it is not silently dropped" -- and its table pins SyGMa (`sygma == 1.1.0`, run in process) and MetaPredictor (weights frozen) as obtained, closing with "what the paper may claim is dominance over the five it did run, named as such". Attempted refutations that fail: (a) "the paper is scoped to MetaTox" -- section 2.1:98 scopes the *population* to where MetaTox predictions exist, and both comparators have predictions on exactly that population; the introduction promises "every budget the comparators are read at" in the plural; (b) "the comparators may be contaminated by these substrates" -- possibly, and that is a reason for a stated caveat, not for silence, and the paper states none. ONE CORRECTION TO THE FINDING: the robust_order block it quotes ("MetaPredictor over GRAIL: dominates true, certified true") is computed against four_method_291.json's own weak GRAIL arm (recall@15 = 0.2647, mean_emitted_uncapped 10.04), not against the deployed configurations of deployment_table, so that quotation does not certify a dominance over the paper's arms; the recall rows above do the work on their own, and no interval on those cross-artifact contrasts has been computed. SEVERITY HELD AT FATAL: the paper's headline is a lead over the weakest of three matched comparators sitting in the release, at budgets where the other two lead it, with the project's own preregistration forbidding exactly this.

findings.title: The abstract's headline sentence splices the whole bank's recall to the trained budget's output size, so it is false under either reading of "the deployed configuration"
findings.where: paper2/grail_service.tex abstract lines 37–39: "Against MetaTox the deployed configuration leads at every budget, with the interval separating at seven of nine, while emitting \numOutputTrained candidates against MetaTox's \numOutputMetatox." (renders as 15.7 vs 31)
findings.problem: No configuration does both. The arm that leads at all nine and separates at seven is the whole bank, whose mean list length is 98.9 — and whose cost envelope fails on 11 of 106 substrates within 600 s (§6). The arm that emits 15.7 is the trained budget, which does not lead at k = 15, 20, 30 or 50 and trails with the interval excluding zero at 20, 30 and 50. §4.1 line 216 defines the deployed service as "what the trained rule budget produces", so the natural reading of "the deployed configuration" is the arm for which the lead claim is false.
findings.evidence: results/deployment_table.json mean_output_length {whole bank 98.9, trained budget 15.7, metatox 31.0}; contrasts trained-budget−metatox at 15 −0.0346 [−0.0762, 0.0065], at 20 −0.0647 [−0.1050, −0.0251], at 30 −0.1113 [−0.1523, −0.0706], at 50 −0.1368 [−0.1846, −0.0917]. paper2/claim.tex lines 1–3 states both arms correctly and separately.
findings.fix: Name the arm in the abstract. If it is the whole bank, print 98.9 as its emission and say the envelope does not finish 11 of 106 substrates in 600 s; if it is the trained budget, print "leads at k ≤ 10 and trails with the interval excluding zero at 20, 30 and 50".
findings.why_it_survived: VERIFIED, and false under both readings. grail_service.tex:37-39 reads "Against MetaTox the deployed configuration leads at every budget, with the interval separating at seven of nine, while emitting $\numOutputTrained$ candidates against MetaTox's $\numOutputMetatox$", rendering as 15.7 against 31. Each half identifies a different arm of results/deployment_table.json. "Leads at every budget" and "separating at seven of nine" fit only the whole bank: its nine gaps are all positive and excludes_zero is true at k = 1, 3, 5, 8, 10, 30, 50 -- exactly seven -- and false at 15 and 20. Its mean_output_length is 98.9. The trained budget's gaps go negative from k=15 (-0.0346, -0.0647, -0.1113, -0.1368), three of them with intervals excluding zero, and eight of its nine cells separate, not seven; its mean_output_length is 15.7, the number printed. So no single configuration satisfies the sentence. The disambiguation runs against the authors: grail_service.tex:216 defines the service as "what the trained rule budget produces", and grail_service.tex:287-289 records that the whole bank leaves 11 of 106 substrates unfinished at 600 s, so the arm that could carry "leads at every budget" is the one the paper says cannot be deployed. paper2/claim.tex:1-3, \input at grail_service.tex:205, states both arms separately and correctly, which shows the correct text exists in the document and the abstract departs from it. Attempted refutation that fails: "the deployed configuration means the whole bank and 15.7 is a stray macro" -- that repairs the lead claim only by making the output-size claim false and contradicting section 4.1 and section 6. SEVERITY HELD AT FATAL: this is the manuscript's headline comparative sentence, it is unsupported as a composite by any arm in deployment_table.json, and the splice runs in the direction that flatters the result -- the whole bank's dominance advertised at the trained budget's list length.

findings.title: The Limitations section states the opposite of Table 1 about which intervals separate at k ≥ 15
findings.where: paper2/grail_service.tex §7 lines 285–286: "At a budget of fifteen and above, the interval on the difference to MetaTox does not separate for either configuration."
findings.problem: Five of the eight arm×budget cells at k ≥ 15 do separate, and the manuscript's own \input{claim} block on the preceding page says so. The false statement is convenient in one direction: it suppresses the three budgets at which the trained budget — the arm §4.1 calls the deployed service — is certifiably behind MetaTox.
findings.evidence: results/deployment_table.json: whole bank − metatox at 30 = 0.0391 [0.0065, 0.0729] excludes_zero true, at 50 = 0.0797 [0.0479, 0.1113] excludes_zero true; trained − metatox at 20 = −0.0647 [−0.1050, −0.0251], at 30 = −0.1113 [−0.1523, −0.0706], at 50 = −0.1368 [−0.1846, −0.0917], all excludes_zero true. paper2/claim.tex line 3: "It trails with the interval excluding zero at k = 20, 30 and 50."
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with the true one: the interval covers zero for the whole bank at k = 15 and 20 and for the trained budget at k = 15, and the trained budget trails with the interval excluding zero at 20, 30 and 50.
findings.why_it_survived: VERIFIED. grail_service.tex:314-315 reads "At a budget of fifteen and above, the interval on the difference to MetaTox does not separate for either configuration. We report the point estimates and the intervals and make no claim there." results/deployment_table.json contradicts this in five of the eight arm-by-budget cells at k >= 15: whole bank - metatox at 30 = 0.0391 [0.0065, 0.0729] excludes_zero true and at 50 = 0.0797 [0.0479, 0.1113] excludes_zero true; trained budget - metatox at 20 = -0.0647 [-0.1050, -0.0251], at 30 = -0.1113 [-0.1523, -0.0706] and at 50 = -0.1368 [-0.1846, -0.0917], all excludes_zero true. Only bank@15, bank@20 and trained@15 fail to separate. The contradiction is internal, not merely with an artifact: paper2/claim.tex, \input one page earlier at grail_service.tex:205, says "the paired-bootstrap interval excluding zero at k = 1, 3, 5, 8, 10, 30 and 50" for the whole bank and "It trails with the interval excluding zero at k = 20, 30 and 50" for the trained budget. The second sentence of the Limitations passage ("make no claim there") is therefore also false of the paper's own claim block. Attempted refutations that fail: (a) reading it as "does not separate in GRAIL's favour" -- bank@30 and bank@50 separate in GRAIL's favour; (b) reading it as covering only k=15 -- the sentence says "fifteen and above", and the brief for this review already exempts the k=15 fact, so what is at issue is the generalisation the authors added to it. The asymmetry matters: the false sentence deletes precisely the three cells where the arm section 4.1 calls the service is certifiably behind MetaTox, and it sits in the section whose function is to disclose them. SEVERITY HELD AT FATAL: a Limitations section that states the opposite of the paper's own table and claim block, in the direction that suppresses the deployed arm's certified deficit, is not a stale-sentence problem a reviewer can wave through.

findings.title: The cap size is printed as a recall: \numHNineCapped is 0.4748, the cap is 100
findings.where: paper2/grail_service.tex line 30-31 (abstract) "capping the candidate pool at $\numHNineCapped$" and line 127-128 (\S3.2) "Keeping the $\numHNineCapped$ highest by generator score before ranking". PDF p.1 and p.3 render "capping the candidate pool at 0.4748" and "Keeping the 0.4748 highest by generator score".
findings.problem: 0.4748 is micro recall@15 under the capped arm, not a pool size. The cap is 100. The same macro is used a second time in the same sentence for its real meaning ("raises micro recall@15 from 0.4489 to 0.4748"), so one macro stands for two different quantities two clauses apart. The correct value appears nowhere in the manuscript as a figure: the only place the cap is named is \S6's word "the hundred that survive the cap". paper2_numbers.py never exports the cap, so no macro exists for it, and check_paper2_numbers.py cannot see the error because the wrong value is a macro and macros are exempt from its literal scan. Verified in the shipped PDF, with one sub-claim of the finding wrong. results/h9_verdict.json has "cap": 100 and "micro": {"uncapped": 0.4489, "capped": 0.4748}; results/deployment_table.json "configuration" also records cap 100. numbers.tex:159 is 
ewcommand{
umHNineCapped}{0.4748} % h9.capped. The manuscript uses that macro as a pool size twice: abstract line 30-31, which the PDF renders "capping the candidate pool at 0.47481" (the 1 is the footnote mark), and section 3.2 line 127, which the PDF renders "Keeping the 0.4748 highest by generator score before ranking, a quantity available before any pair graph is built, raises micro recall@15 from 0.4489 to 0.4748" - one macro standing for two different quantities in a single sentence. So the sentence generalises one true cell over a range where the deployed arm is certified to lose three times, and calls those losses "no claim there". I could not find a reading that rescues it. The finding's closing claim that "the only place the reader can find the truth is claim.tex" is an overstatement - line 208 of the body also says "Above ten it trails" - which is why I put this at major rather than fatal: it is a self-contradiction correctable in one sentence, not a loss the manuscript hides. findings.title: Half the Results section is measured on the comparison population and the paper labels only the other half
findings.where: paper2/grail_service.tex §3.4 lines 148–175 (H8's −0.1203/−0.0647/−0.0556; the decode ladder 0.5023→0.385; the oracle 0.3549/0.6692/0.3654; H12's +0.0286; H14's −0.0286/−0.0361), read immediately after lines 117, 128–129 and 139 which say "on a held-out split" three times

findings.evidence: results/h8_verdict.json population = {n: 291, source: 'the 291 of results/four_method_291.json'}; results/h12_verdict.json and results/h14_verdict.json, same; results/group_decode.json population n=291; results/wide_pool_analysis_implicit.json population n=291. findings.why_it_survived: UPHELD. Verified directly. §3.1–3.3 say "On a held-out split" (l.117), "the held-out split" (l.128–129), "On the held-out split" (l.139), and their artifacts declare split="validation", n_substrates=293, n_references=655 (h7/h9/h10_verdict.json). Every number in §3.4 comes from an artifact declaring population {n: 291, source: 'the 291 of results/four_method_291.json'}: h8_verdict.json (-0.1203/-0.0647/-0.0556), h12_verdict.json (+0.0286 and its ceiling), h14_verdict.json (-0.0286/-0.0361), group_decode.json (the 0.5023->0.385 ladder), wide_pool_analysis_implicit.json (0.3549/0.6692/0.3654, the _micro fields). §3.4 names no population anywhere in lines 148-175, so the label set three times in the three preceding subsections carries forward and is wrong. That the two populations give different baselines is visible in the paper's own macros: fusion@15 is 0.4489 on validation (l.117) and 0.5023 on the 291 (l.158), unexplained. Two aggravations I checked myself and that the finding does not mention: (a) wide_pool_analysis_implicit.json's score_combinations_at_15_micro holds exactly four combinations (product/filter/generator/rrf) on the 291 — that is the argmax the manuscript alludes to at l.119-121 without naming, so §3.4's baseline sits on the selection population; (b) group_decode.json's own status field reads "UPPER BOUND. The round-robin rule was chosen after reading the oracle decomposition on these same 291 substrates. It must be registered and checked on the validation split before it is quoted as a result", and l.156-158 quotes it as a result. Attempted refutations that failed: §2.1 (l.98-102) does establish that none of the 291 was trained or selected on, so the numbers are not invalid — but that paragraph is two sections away and labels the *comparison* population, not §3.4; nothing in §3.4 points to it. The finding's supporting claim about the gate is also correct: scripts/check_coverage.py line 30 is PAPER = ROOT/"paper"/"grail_iclr.tex", and I ran scripts/population_matching_scan.py --paper paper2 — it reports "0 paragraph(s) compare across more than one population", because scan_prose only fires when a paragraph names MORE THAN ONE population (line 68: if len(names) > 1) and paper2 prints populations through macros, not literals. The gate is structurally blind to the defect, which is an omission rather than a collision. Fix is one clause per subsection. Severity major: half the Results is silently reattributed to the wrong split by the reader.

findings.title: "running in under two seconds per substrate" comes from a 40-substrate exploratory draw and contradicts the paper's own cost section
findings.where: paper2/grail_service.tex lines 207–208: "The trained budget leads at the tight budgets while returning lists half the length of MetaTox's and running in under two seconds per substrate."
findings.problem: The number is 1.85 s from results/rule_budget_curve.json, whose own status field reads "EXPLORATORY. A curve, not a hypothesis. The operating point read off it must be fixed by a stated rule and checked where it was not chosen", and whose population is 40 substrates carrying 92 references drawn from the 291. It is a bare word-number with no macro, in a file whose header states 'A number that is not here may not appear in the manuscript', and it sits four pages from a §Cost section reporting a median of 49.85 s before and 5.28 s after the two fixes, and an envelope in which 11 of 106 substrates do not finish in 600 s. Nothing tells the reader that 1.85 s is a different arm, a different population, a different cache state and a different machine.
findings.evidence: results/rule_budget_curve.json: status as quoted; population = {n: 40, n_references: 92, drawn_from: 'the 291'}; by_rule_budget['30'].s_per_substrate = 1.85. results/h15_verdict.json time.h15_median_s = 5.28; results/h13_verdict.json time.every_product_median_s = 49.85. results/cost_envelope.json: 11 of 106 unfinished at 600 s. paper2/numbers.tex header line 2.
findings.fix: Either drop the claim or promote it to a macro with its population and arm stated: 'at the trained budget, 1.85 s per substrate on a 40-substrate draw'. Reconcile it in the same paragraph with the 5.28 s median of §Cost.
findings.why_it_survived: UPHELD, though not for every reason given. Verified: grep across all 254 result JSONs finds 1.85 in exactly one place — results/rule_budget_curve.json, by_rule_budget['30'].s_per_substrate — whose population block reads {n: 40, n_references: 92, seed: 0, drawn_from: 'the 291'}. Line 207-208 attaches it to a sentence whose other two clauses ("leads at the tight budgets", "lists half the length of MetaTox's") are both measured on the 291, so the population changes mid-sentence with no marker. The number is a MEAN over 40 substrates of a heavy-tailed quantity — cost_envelope.json shows per-substrate cost spanning 0.6 s to unfinished-at-600 s — and 1.85 sits 8% under the threshold the prose asserts, so a draw of 40 that happens to miss the tail is exactly where an underestimate hides; nothing bounds it on the 291. It also evades the manuscript's own discipline: numbers.tex line 2 says "A number that is not here may not appear in the manuscript", there is no macro for it, and I ran scripts/check_paper2_numbers.py — it returns OK because its literal scan (line 48) matches digits only, so a spelled-out "two seconds" is invisible to it. Two of the finding's supporting arguments are weaker than stated and I do not rest on them: the EXPLORATORY status's stated concern is that the operating point read off the curve be fixed by a stated rule and checked elsewhere, which the preregistration does answer (30 is the checkpoint's recorded top_k, checked on validation as H10); and the §Cost figures (49.85 s -> 5.28 s median, 11 of 106 unfinished) are the whole-bank arm on validation, so they do not literally contradict 1.85 s at the trained budget. The surviving defect is a bare, unqualified deployment-cost claim — the paper's only statement of what the service costs per molecule, which is a headline attribute for an applications venue — supported by a 40-substrate exploratory subsample with no population, no interval, no machine or cache state, and no macro. Fix: measure it on the 291, or say "about 1.85 s on a 40-substrate draw".

findings.title: The abstract promises an interval on every difference; most differences in the Results carry none
findings.where: paper2/grail_service.tex line 25 "with a paired bootstrap on each difference", against lines 155–158, 163–167, 170–174, 225–226, 269–272
findings.problem: A universal quantifier the body does not honour, and the intervals exist unused in the artifacts. Reported without intervals: H8's −0.1203, −0.0647 and −0.0556 (artifact has [−0.1590,−0.0828], [−0.1008,−0.0292], [−0.0969,−0.0166]); H14's −0.0286 and −0.0361 (artifact has [−0.0558,−0.0044], [−0.0576,−0.0147]); H12's 'ceiling' 0.0286 ([0.0156,0.0431]); the decode ladder 0.5023→0.385 (group_decode.json carries contrasts); the oracle 0.3549→0.6692; the H11 recall comparison 0.5406 vs 0.5672 (h11_grid.json has no ci at all, and the 'loses 0 of 55 cells' claim is a count of point estimates with no interval anywhere); H13/H15's −0.0015 ([−0.0124, 0.0081]). The paper's own checklist row 4 requires exactly this.
findings.evidence: results/h8_verdict.json primary_scorer_minus_fusion.ci95, what_the_design_costs_before_the_model_acts.ci95, what_the_model_adds_given_the_design.ci95; results/h14_verdict.json primary_gate_minus_cap.ci95, ceiling_of_this_gate.ci95; results/h12_verdict.json ceiling_of_this_composition.ci95; results/h13_verdict.json recall_contrasts['15'].ci95; results/h11_grid.json (no ci95 key anywhere). paper/SELF_CLAIMS.md row 4.

findings.why_it_survived: UPHELD, but heavily narrowed; most of the enumerated list is refuted. Refuted: the abstract's promise (l.25) is scoped to the MetaTox sweep — "evaluated against MetaTox on 291 substrates ... at every output budget the field reports, with a paired bootstrap on each difference" — and deployment_table.json carries ci95 and excludes_zero on every contrast at every one of the nine budgets, with claim.tex reporting which separate; the table caption (l.201-202) states "Intervals on every difference are in the released artifact". §2.1's sentence (l.95-96) claims the bootstrap is computed, not printed, and it is: H8's three gaps, H12's ceiling, H14's two gaps, H13/H15's -0.0015 and group_decode's ladder contrasts all carry ci95 in their released artifacts, exactly as the finding itself documents. Reporting a point estimate whose released interval excludes zero overstates nothing. What survives, and I verified it: two comparisons carry no interval ANYWHERE. (a) h11_grid.json has no ci95 key at any depth (grep returns nothing), so §4.1's "loses 0 of 55 cells" (l.221) is a count of point estimates and "its macro recall is 0.5406 against the rule's 0.5672" (l.224-226) has no interval in the paper or the record — and that sentence is the one the paper offers as "the component that is not open to that objection", i.e. it is load-bearing. I checked the alternatives: 0.5672/0.5406 appear in no artifact carrying an interval, and emission_leaderboard.json's paired_f1_contrasts_vs_rule are on a different population (n=150, artifacts/tier2/substrates.json). (b) wide_pool_analysis_implicit.json carries no interval either, so the oracle headroom 0.3549 -> 0.6692, quoted twice including in Limitations (l.317) as the basis for "we do not know whether a mechanism outside those two reaches it", has none. Against the universal at l.95-96 ("every difference carries a 95% paired bootstrap") those two are counterexamples, and the project's own SELF_CLAIMS row 4 demands the interval on the difference. Fix: bootstrap those two, or name the exceptions in §2.1. Minor, not major: no conclusion in the paper is overturned by the omission, and every difference the paper rests a verdict on already has its interval in the released record.

findings.title: The Availability claim about provenance is falsified by the provenance artifact itself
findings.where: paper2/grail_service.tex lines 302–303: "Each reported artifact carries the hash of the code that wrote it, and a sweep refuses any artifact whose producer has changed since it was written."
findings.problem: Three ways false. (a) The sweep is empty: results/artifact_provenance.json has "sweep": {} and "sweep_not_current": [], because the audit was run without --all, so it examined only 38 pinned files out of ~294 in results/ and swept zero others. (b) It did not refuse: n_pinned_stale = 2, and both stale entries — typed_edit_known_pairs.json and typed_edit_known_type_recovery.json, which back §5's 98/40/337/475 decomposition — are marked producer_changed with the diff recorded. The script returns exit 1 on that state; the committed artifact records a failing run. (c) Two artifacts the manuscript reports from carry no provenance block at all: results/coverage_gap_types.json, the source of the headline ceiling 0.8171 and of every number in §5's first paragraph, and results/external_overlap_audit.json, the source of the leakage audit in §2.1. Not pinned and not swept: cost_envelope.json, reaction_timeout_probe.json, rule_budget_curve.json, wide_pool_analysis_implicit.json.
findings.evidence: results/artifact_provenance.json: n_pinned 38, n_pinned_stale 2, sweep {}, sweep_not_current []; the two producer_changed rows. scripts/audit_artifact_provenance.py lines 116, 139–151 (sweep only under --all) and 163 (`return 1` on stale pinned). `python3 -c` dump showing coverage_gap_types.json and external_overlap_audit.json have no 'provenance' key.
findings.fix: Re-run the audit with --all, stamp coverage_gap_types.py and external_overlap_audit.py, pin the cost and curve artifacts the paper reads, and either fix the two stale producers or state in Availability that two artifacts' producers have moved and what the diff was.
findings.why_it_survived: UPHELD on legs (a) and (c); leg (b) is FALSE and must be dropped. Leg (b) refuted: results/artifact_provenance.json in the working tree has n_pinned 38, n_pinned_stale 0, and every one of the 38 pinned entries carries status "current" — including typed_edit_known_pairs.json and typed_edit_known_type_recovery.json, which the finding claims are stale. The string "producer_changed" appears nowhere in the artifact (only at scripts/audit_artifact_provenance.py:152). I also checked HEAD (git show HEAD:results/artifact_provenance.json): n_pinned 15, n_pinned_stale 0, sweep {}. So there is no failing run recorded, committed or working-tree, and the script's `return 1` path was not taken. Leg (a) verified: sweep is {} and sweep_not_current is [] in both copies, and the sweep over unpinned files runs only under --all (audit_artifact_provenance.py, `if args.all:` guarding the glob over results/*.json); 38 of the 254 JSONs in results/ are pinned, so the released record shows zero artifacts swept. Leg (c) verified and it is the strongest: results/coverage_gap_types.json and results/external_overlap_audit.json have no "provenance" key at all, and scripts/paper2_numbers.py reads coverage_gap_types.json at line 36 and external_overlap_audit.json at line 40 — they are the source of the ceiling 0.8171 and of 475/98/40/337 in §5, and of the 24-of-37 GLORYx overlap the paper leans on at l.100-102 as proof that it audits rather than assumes. So l.331-332's "Each reported artifact carries the hash of the code that wrote it" is false for the two artifacts behind the paper's stated bound and its leakage audit, and "a sweep refuses any artifact whose producer has changed" describes a capability the released record shows was never exercised beyond the pinned 38. (The finding's "not pinned and not swept" list — cost_envelope, reaction_timeout_probe, rule_budget_curve, wide_pool_analysis_implicit — is half wrong: all four do carry their own provenance blocks; they are merely outside the pinned set.) Fix: stamp the two artifacts and re-run the audit with --all, or restrict the sentence to the pinned set. Major: it is a false universal about exactly the evidence the reader is asked to trust.

findings.title: "The failures are ordinary drug-sized molecules" is false of the largest failure
findings.where:
paper2/grail_service.tex lines 258–260: "At the whole bank, $
umEnvelopeUnfinished$ of $
umEnvelopeN$ substrates do not finish within $
umEnvelopeDeadline$ seconds, and the smallest that fails carries $
umEnvelopeSmallestUnfinished$ heavy atoms. The failures are ordinary drug-sized molecules, so the envelope is not an exotic case."

findings.why_it_survived:
Stands, verified arithmetically. h15_verdict.json load_correction gives speedup_attributable_to_the_budget = 2.52, and 2.52 = (unbounded_arm_standardise_median_s 11.88 / standardise_survivors_median_s 2.73) / load_factor 1.73 = 4.35/1.73 -- the load-corrected ratio of the STANDARDISATION step between the two survivors arms. The preregistration states the numerator ('Dividing that out of the standardisation's 4.35 leaves 2.52'); the manuscript does not. numbers.tex carries only 
umHOneFiveLoad (1.73), 
umHOneFiveAttributable (2.52) and 
umHOneFiveTime (5.28) -- no macro for 11.88, 2.73 or 4.35 -- so no quantity the paper prints, divided by 1.73, yields 2.52. REFUTED sub-claim: predicted_by_the_budget_curve 3.93 vs measured 2.52 is discussed in the preregistration and its absence from a six-page manuscript is not a defect.

findings.title: The ceiling quoted as bounding the comparison is measured on a different population than the comparison
findings.where: paper2/grail_service.tex line 42 (abstract) "The bound on all of this is the rule bank's coverage, $\numCeilingCoverage$ of annotated transformations" and line 230 "The bank reaches $\numCeilingCoverage$ of annotated transformations on the test split."

findings.title: MetaTox is not read at its own emission; the output-matched arm is in the artifact and unused, and the analysis silently truncates MetaTox at 50
findings.where: paper2/grail_service.tex §4 lines 180–182 ("MetaTox is read from its own predictions with no cap imposed by us. Mean list lengths are 98.9, 15.7 and 31") and §4.1 lines 220–226 ("Compared at each method's own emission…"); scripts/typed_edit/deployment_table.py line 75
findings.problem: Both statements are wrong. (a) deployment_table.py applies `_dedup(mtx.get(s, []), max(KS))`, i.e. it truncates every MetaTox list at 50 — that is a cap imposed by the analysis, and it is why the same quantity prints as 31 in §4 and 36.34 in §4.1. (b) MetaTox's own emission policy is PASS's declared Pa > Pi threshold, recorded in the ingest artifact as `predictions_above_own_threshold` with `mean_output_above_threshold: 17.79`; the paper reads the unthresholded list instead. Recomputing MetaTox at its own threshold on the same 291 substrates with the same keys gives a mean emission of 15.76 — matched to the trained budget's 15.7 — and recall {1:0.0406, 3:0.1323, 5:0.2150, 8:0.2977, 10:0.3609, 15:0.4692, 20:0.4842, 30:0.4872, 50:0.4917}. Against that output-matched arm the trained budget's k=15 deficit and its three certified losses at 20/30/50 all disappear. The paper's §4.1 defence ("That comparison is biased toward the smaller emitter … our rule emits less than half as much") is an artefact of the unmatched arm the paper chose: at MetaTox's own emission the two sides emit the same amount.
findings.evidence: results/metatox_smirks_preds.json: mean_output 36.43, mean_output_above_threshold 17.79, field `predictions_above_own_threshold` built as `[t[0] for t in v if t[1] > t[2]]` in scripts/metatox_smirks_ingest.py (Pa > Pi, PASS's own threshold). scripts/typed_edit/deployment_table.py line 75: `"metatox": {s: _dedup(mtx.get(s, []), max(KS)) for s in subs}` with KS = (1,3,5,8,10,15,20,30,50). Recomputed thresholded curve above, using the same `_dedup`/key table the deployment table uses.
findings.fix: Add MetaTox's own thresholded emission as a third column (it is the only output-matched arm available), state the 50-truncation, and reconcile the 31 vs 36.34 discrepancy between §4 and §4.1.
findings.why_it_survived: Stands; I reproduced it exactly. Using the same key table (results/key_tables/inchikey_tautomer.json), the same _dedup, and the same population the deployment table builds (291 substrates, 665 references), MetaTox's full list gives {1:0.0406, 3:0.1323, 5:0.218, 8:0.3113, 10:0.388, 15:0.5143, 20:0.5519, 30:0.6015, 50:0.6271} -- identical to Table 1's MetaTox column, so my pipeline matches the paper's; MetaTox's predictions_above_own_threshold gives mean emission 15.76 (against the trained budget's 15.7) and {1:0.0406, 3:0.1323, 5:0.215, 8:0.2977, 10:0.3609, 15:0.4692, 20:0.4842, 30:0.4872, 50:0.4917}. Against that output-matched arm the trained budget (0.4797/0.4872/0.4902/0.4902 at k=15/20/30/50) ties or leads at every budget, so its k=15 deficit and its certified losses at 20/30/50 are entirely against records PASS declined to score. The undisclosed material fact I verified directly: 5,423 of the 10,601 MetaTox records the paper counts carry no PASS spectrum at all, and metatox_smirks_ingest.py itself reads the absence of a spectrum as below PASS's own threshold ('PASS writes the spectrum only where it clears its own threshold, and says so in a second tag' -- the ingest raises if the two tags disagree), then ranks those unscored records after the scored ones in file order. Nothing in §4 or §4.1 tells the reader this; §4.1's 'each method's own emission' column for MetaTox is h11_grid's 'uncapped' 36.34, while the same repo's ingest artifact carries mean_output_above_threshold 17.79 unused. Three corrections to the finding. (i) The _dedup(..., max(KS)) truncation at 50 is real but non-binding: recall@k for k<=50 never reads past position 50, so it changes no reported recall or short-list count -- only the printed mean list length, which is why §4 prints 31 and §4.1 prints 36.34 for the same quantity. That inconsistency is worth fixing; it is not a cap on the comparison. (ii) §4.1 is not silent on matching -- it reports MetaTox truncated at k=15, macro recall 0.5406 against the rule's 0.5672; what is missing is the arm defined by the comparator's own threshold. (iii) The unmatched arm is not self-serving: counting the unscored half helps MetaTox and costs the trained budget above k=15. Separate defect found while checking these cells: Limitations lines 313-314 say 'At a budget of fifteen and above, the interval on the difference to MetaTox does not separate for either configuration', but numbers.tex has gap.bank.30.sep=yes, gap.bank.50.sep=yes and gap.trained.20/30/50.sep=yes -- contradicting the abstract's own 'separating at seven of nine'.

missed.title: Training-seed variance was measured over three retrained checkpoints and is reported nowhere, although it is the size of several gaps the paper certifies

missed.evidence: results/h11_grid.json, criterion inchikey_tautomer: the rule's precision is 0.1026 (recall 0.5672, F1 0.1530); MetaTox's is 0.1037 at k=3, 0.1022 at k=5, 0.0909 at k=10 and 0.0837 at k=15. The same file carries precision for all five criteria and ten budgets. No precision figure appears in paper2/numbers.tex.

missed.title: Eighteen simultaneous intervals are read without any multiplicity control, which the paper's own preregistration mandates

missed.problem: Nothing in the manuscript mentions multiplicity, and no correction is applied in the artifact that produces the table. A count of separations over eighteen uncorrected 95% intervals is exactly the statistic multiplicity control exists for, and "seven of nine" is being used as evidence of a sweep-wide result. The preregistration commits the project to the opposite discipline in its opening paragraph, and the paper neither applies it nor states that each budget is being read marginally.
missed.evidence: paper2/preregistration.md, line 10: "Multiplicity is corrected with Holm inside a declared family, and each hypothesis names its own." scripts/typed_edit/deployment_table.py computes a bare 2.5/97.5 quantile per cell (lines 84–99) with no correction and no family declaration; results/deployment_table.json records only per-cell ci95 and excludes_zero. missed.title: Nine of the fifteen registered hypotheses are reported and the Availability section's claim about the preregistration is false for the other six

missed.claim: The paper's first contribution bullet is preregistration discipline, and Availability tells the reader the released preregistration carries an outcome for every hypothesis.
missed.problem: The preregistration registers fifteen hypotheses. Only H7–H15 carry an "Outcome" section; H1 through H6 — the label-space hypothesis, informed node features, learned abstention, the ranked prediction of intervention sizes, the out-of-sample null and the negative control — carry a prediction, a failure criterion and no result. missed.evidence: grep "Outcome" paper2/preregistration.md returns exactly nine hits, at lines 390, 492, 571, 636, 730, 806, 908, 982 and 1070, all inside the H7–H15 sections (lines 357–1105). H1 (line 287) and H2–H6 (lines 1106–1268) have Prediction / Failure / Family blocks and no Outcome.

missed.evidence: grep "cite" paper2/grail_service.tex returns one line (110, \citep{cormack2009}); paper2/refs.bib holds 50 entries including Ridder_2008, Djoumbou_Feunang_2019, de_Bruyn_Kops_2020, Litsa_2020, Zhu_2024, Larsson_2025, Zhou_2025, Zhou_2026 and Chavan_2026, none cited. paper2/preregistration.md §0.3: "A comparator that cannot be obtained by the freeze is reported in the paper as unavailable, with the reason; it is not silently dropped", with the ten-row table and results/comparator_acquisition.json recording the URL and date behind each fact.
missed.fix: Add a related-work section citing the field's systems, and a comparator-availability paragraph reproducing the preregistration's table: which comparators were pinned, which were frozen, and which could not be run as released with the reason for each.

missed.problem: Released where, under what licence, at what version? The section contains no URL, no DOI, no repository name and no licence statement, and the repository state does not support the claim. artifacts/ and results/ are both gitignored, only 18 files under artifacts/ are tracked, and the generator and filter checkpoints the paper's numbers come from are not among them — the single tracked .pt is an unrelated factorized model. No LICENSE file at the repository root; no license or url key in pyproject.toml. README.md line 227: "the package does not ship giant checkpoints by default. For publication, weights should be versioned separately, for example via Zenodo". paper2/preregistration.md §0.2: "The dataset is external and cannot live in the repository".
missed.fix: Give the repository URL, an archival DOI, a licence for code and for artifacts, and the commit or release tag; state exactly which of the listed items are actually distributed, where the checkpoints are deposited, and how a reader obtains the external dataset.

missed.title: The paper never states how many biotransformation steps its predictions cover, and the multi-step measurements it has are not reported
missed.where: paper2/grail_service.tex §2 lines 81–85 (the three-stage description) and §5 lines 281–283 ("Closing this gap needs new annotated metabolic chemistry")
missed.claim: The system applies selected templates and enumerates products; §5 concludes that the uncovered 337 references need chemistry no template library supplies.
missed.problem: Metabolism is sequential — phase I then phase II — and every comparator in this field emits multi-generation metabolites. The manuscript never says whether GRAIL applies one round of templates or several, so a reader cannot tell whether the comparison is matched on generations or whether the coverage gap is novel chemistry or uncomposed known chemistry. The project has measured both and reports neither, which leaves §5's conclusion resting on an unstated premise.
missed.evidence: results/benchmark_report_depth2.json: depth-1 ceiling 0.7292 (tautomer) against a depth-2 lower bound of 0.7231 on the same 150 substrates, lift_over_depth1 0.0123. results/composition_recovery.json (n_substrates 1170, inchikey_tautomer): composing through predicted intermediates recovers 0.86% of GRAIL's missed references, CI [0.0041, 0.0138], against MetaPredictor's 2.43% and SyGMa's 1.36%, with GRAIL below MetaPredictor by 0.0158 [−0.0249, −0.0069]. Neither file is cited in paper2/grail_service.tex or paper2/numbers.tex; the words "step", "generation" and "depth" appear in the manuscript only in unrelated senses.
missed.fix: State the number of generations the pipeline enumerates and the number each comparator emits, and add the depth-2 and composition measurements to §5 so the claim that the residual gap is novel chemistry is supported rather than assumed.

missed.title: The two configurations are never compared on cost, so the paper's central deployment decision is asserted without evidence
missed.where: paper2/grail_service.tex §4 line 179 ("Both configurations, the whole bank and the trained budget"), §4.1 line 216 ("the service returns what the trained rule budget produces"), §6 lines 287–289
missed.claim: Two configurations are presented as co-equal deployable arms in Table 1, and §4.1 then declares that the service ships the trained budget.
missed.problem: No reason is given for that choice anywhere in the text. §3.3 compares the two arms on recall and pool size only; §6 measures the cost of a different change — whole-product versus survivors standardisation — never bank versus trained budget; and the one fact that would decide it, that the whole bank fails to finish on roughly a tenth of substrates within ten minutes, is reported three pages later without being connected to the arm that produces Table 1's leading column. The reader is told which arm ships and never why, and is left believing both arms are servable.
missed.evidence: §6 line 287–289 reports 11 of 106 substrates unfinished within 600 seconds at the whole bank; paper2/preregistration.md H13 records that the whole-product arm "has never finished in any run at any budget" on the 291-heavy-atom substrate, while the survivors arm completed all 294. The per-arm cost the decision needs exists in results/rule_budget_curve.json (1.85 s at the trained budget against 56.67 s at a budget of 100, quoted in preregistration H10) and is never reported per arm in the manuscript.

missed.title: No execution environment is given for any timing, and the four cost measurements come from four different populations that the section never names
missed.claim: The section reports 11 of 106 unfinished within 600 s, 5.2 seconds to apply all templates to a 109-heavy-atom substrate, about four thousand standardisations per substrate, a median moving from 49.85 s to 16.92 s to 5.28 s, and a load ratio of 1.73.
missed.problem: Not one of these numbers carries a machine or a software stack: no CPU, no core count, no memory, no parallelism, no RDKit or Python version, no cache state. The section itself concedes that load differed between arms and divides a factor out, which makes the missing environment the difference between a measurement and an anecdote. The four figures also come from four different populations and runs — a seven-substrate probe, a forty-substrate curve, a 106-substrate sampled envelope and a 293-substrate validation pass — and the text presents them as one narrative without naming any of them.
missed.evidence: results/generator_cost_split.json contains 7 rows, with n_normalize_calls ranging 366 to 4,976 (the source of "about four thousand" and of the 5.2 s / 109-atom figure, both hard-coded literals in the .tex rather than macros from paper2/numbers.tex). results/cost_envelope.json: split validation, sample_every 3, n_done 106. results/h13_verdict.json and results/h15_verdict.json are over 293 validation substrates. No provenance block in any of these records hardware or library versions.
missed.fix: Add a one-line environment statement (CPU model, cores used, RAM, OS, Python and RDKit versions, cache state) and label each timing with the population it was measured on and its size.

missed.title: A mean pool size is attributed to the median substrate, and no dispersion is reported for any cost or pool quantity
missed.where: paper2/grail_service.tex §3.2 line 126: "The bank enumerates 669.9 candidates for the median substrate"
missed.claim: 669.9 candidates is presented as the median substrate's pool.
missed.problem: 669.9 is a mean, not a median, and the distribution it summarises is strongly skewed, so the two are far apart. The paper reports no dispersion anywhere for pool size or cost — no IQR, no maximum — even though the skew is the whole reason the cap and the cost work exist, and the preregistration quotes a worst case nearly seven times the mean.
missed.evidence: results/h9_verdict.json records the quantity under the key "mean_pool": {"uncapped": 669.9, "capped": 98.0} over 293 validation substrates, and paper2/numbers.tex tags the macro \numHNinePoolBefore as h9.pool.before. paper2/preregistration.md H9: "588.7 candidates on average over the deployment population, 4,614 at the worst".
